subject: BankWave post-call recap — cost levers, pilot SOW & procurement asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: James O'Neill <j.oneill@bankwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BankWave post-call recap — cost levers, pilot SOW & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, James — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of BankWave pain / goals (as I heard them)
- Primary pain: inference spend is growing non-linearly as token volumes scale; procurement has a hard cap for Q2 of ~$45k/mo.
- Operational goals: p95 latency target <= 100ms for the critical fraud-check route; avoid 2–3s tail spikes that impact UX.
- Business goal: validate a path to < $0.0007 per inference call at scale (10M tokens/mo target) while keeping data residency and audit controls intact.

Key cost levers we discussed (impacts are illustrative; we'll quantify with your token distribution)
- Batching: continuous micro-batching for short requests; expected 15–35% token compute savings depending on concurrency.
- Prefix/KV caching: de-duplicate repeated context for user sessions — typical 10–25% reductions on chat-style workflows.
- Model variant routing & quantization: use an FP16/8 quantized variant for non-sensitive routes (2–3x speedups in inference ops; unit-cost reduction).
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated): commit to a pool for peak traffic to get predictable lower unit pricing vs hosted bursts.

Immediate asks from us to size an accurate TCO:
1) Monthly token counts (tokens per month and distribution by endpoint/route).
2) Peak qps and expected concurrency windows (UTC).
3) Example request/response samples (redacted) so we can estimate KV cache hit-rate.

Proposed pilot (minimal-risk, quantifiable)
- Scope: 2-week pilot with a single critical endpoint (fraud-check route) limited to 100k queries; compare baseline hosted vs Redwood Dedicated-backed routing with caching enabled.
- Deliverables: pilot SOW, TCO workbook with committed vs hosted scenarios, latency/cost dashboards, and a short summary of expected steady-state savings.
- Success metrics: >=20% unit-cost reduction OR p95 <=100ms with equivalent quality.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-sow.pdf (pilot SOW draft), bankwave-tco-estimates.xlsx (placeholder TCO).

Next steps
- James / Elaine: share token volumes + sample payloads by EOD next Tue (Apr 12) if possible.
- Redwood: we will return a populated TCO workbook and a short SOW draft within 3 business days after we receive the data.
- Suggested meeting: procurement + security sync (30 min) the week of Apr 12 to cover SOC2, data residency, and commercial terms.

If any item above is off, please ping and I'll update. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the TCO assumptions.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

1) Can you provide a line-item monthly estimate for 10M tokens across two scenarios: a) pure hosted (pay-as-you-go) and b) 12-month reserved commit with expected savings? Please include latency tiers (p95 expectations) in each scenario.
2) Security/compliance: we need your SOC 2 attestation and a short note on data residency — BankWave's EU customers must keep PII in eu-west-1.
3) Contracting: we prefer PO/invoice flow. If there are any standard redlines Redwood doesn't accept, flag them early.
4) Pilot SOW: procurement wants a one-page SOW with start/end dates, acceptance criteria, and a capped spend for the pilot (we prefer a firm not-to-exceed number).

Timeline: procurement aiming to issue a PO by end of May; security review will happen in parallel but likely needs a small call with your security team.

If you can get the TCO workbook back with the two scenarios and the one-pager SOW, I can route to Elaine/Procurement and circle back with questions.

Cheers,
James

Appreciate the quick reply, James — answers inline below and an explicit pilot invoice cap we can sign to.

On 10M tokens (illustrative baseline ranges)
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.0085 per 1k tokens baseline compute + infra (depends on model variant). At 10M tokens this maps to ~ $85/month purely compute (this is a simplified number — we will fill the TCO with per-route breakdown).
- Reserved/Committed (12-month uplift): typical committed discounts are ~25–40% depending on utilization and burst allowance; for a steady 10M tokens/month, expected effective unit cost reduction ~35% relative to hosted.
- Latency: hosted burst can meet 100–200ms p95 depending on load; Dedicated + optimized batching/cache typically gives the most consistent p95 <= 100ms for sustained traffic.

Pilot SOW (one-pager summary) — highlights
- Duration: 2 weeks (start target Apr 19)
- Scope: fraud-check endpoint only, up to 100k queries total
- Deliverables: TCO workbook (hosted vs reserved), latency/cost dashboards, simple findings doc
- Acceptance: ability to demonstrate >=20% unit-cost reduction OR p95 <= 100ms vs baseline
- Spend cap: $2,500 (not-to-exceed) for the pilot — Redwood will invoice if cap is hit; otherwise we prorate.

Security & procurement items we can provide right away
- SOC 2 Type II report (we will share the redacted report link).
- Data residency: we support region pinning (eu-west-1) for Private deployments; for hosted flows we can pin model execution region and provide audit logs.
- Contracting: we accept PO/invoice; I will flag any uncommon redline items if they arise.

Attachments included: redwood-pilot-sow.pdf (one-pager), bankwave-tco-estimates.xlsx (initial scenario sheet). I pushed a short SOC2 pointer to the drive link in related_links.

Proposed next step: Can we book a 30-minute procurement + security sync next Tue Apr 12 at 11:00 AM PT? If that works, I'll invite our legal/security and Marissa (commercial lead) to join.

If that timing is tight, propose two windows and we will accommodate.

Thanks — I'll get the detailed TCO back within 2 business days after your token numbers.

Best,
Karthik

Redwood Inference
